songs.name: Beat It On Down The Line

ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Winterland set with soaring Dark Star>Stella Blue and tight Mississippi Half‑Step
ai_show_review.blurb: Features a smoking Dark Star into Stella Blue alongside a crisp Mississippi Half‑Step Uptown Toodeloo. China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider launches the first set with bright momentum, while He's Gone delivers punchy drive. Multiple sources capture the high energy; the matrix mix offers the cleanest listening experience.
ai_show_review.review:
The December 11, 1972 Winterland show captures the Dead in top form, riding a wave of inspiration that rolls from the opening numbers straight into one of their most memorable second‑set peaks. The set opens solidly with The Promised Land and a rolling string of classics before China Cat Sunflower segues into I Know You Rider, a bright, lyrical pairing that launches the band into an exuberant groove. From there the group builds momentum through Box of Rain, He's Gone and Around & Around, each song landing with crisp rhythm section tightness. 

The second set is where the night truly shines: Mississippi Half‑Step Uptown Toodeloo grooves with Keith’s shimmering keys, and Dark Star erupts into a soaring, exploratory journey that seamlessly folds into Stella Blue—one of the era's most electric transitions. The band stays locked in through Big River, Deal, Tomorrow Is Forever and a joyous Sugar Magnolia, ending the night on a high note with Casey Jones. Across all recordings the performance is consistently high‑energy, and the matrix mix (Dusborne) delivers the clearest capture of this magic, preserving every nuance from Jerry’s bright Strat leads to Bill’s steady drumming.

best_recording.reason: Excellent matrix mix with crystal‑clear balance, minimal glitches, and full capture of the Dark Star>Stella Blue sequence.

key_highlights: Smoking Dark Star segue into Stella Blue – a soaring, exploratory centerpiece.
Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo – tight groove with shimmering keyboards.
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider – bright first‑set pairing that launches the energy.
He's Gone – powerful early‑set anthem delivered with punchy rhythm section.

band_performance.Jerry: Bright Strat tone drives the night; his leads on Dark Star and Stella Blue are incisive and soaring, while vocal moments add extra color.
band_performance.Phil: Solid bass foundation underpins every jam; praised for a steady groove on Mississippi Half‑Step and supportive low end throughout.
band_performance.Bob: Rhythm guitar locks in tightly, exfiltrating Jerry’s leads and adding momentum to He's Gone and the early set flow.
band_performance.Keith: Consistently strong keyboard work, providing shimmering textures on Mississippi Half‑Step and enriching the Dark Star improvisation.
band_performance.Bill: Steady drumming keeps the band grounded; despite being a bit recessed in some audience tapes, his groove remains tight throughout.
